श्राद्धकल्प: Śrāddhakalpa — the rituals prescribed as due to Pitṛs. M. 2. 23.
श्राद्धद: Śrāddhada — a son of Vṛṣa. Br. III. 6. 34.
श्राद्धदेव: Śrāddhadeva (I) — a tīrtha on the Sarasvatī. Bhā. III. 1. 22.
Śrāddhadeva (II) — a son of Niṣādajara. Br. 71. 120.

Śrāddhadeva (III) — (Manu: a son of Vivasvata and Samjñā: Seventh Manu (s.v.) Manu Vaivasvata. Satyavrata in previous birth. Bhā. VI. 6. 40; VIII. 13. 1 and 9; 24. 11; Br. III. 63. 215; Vi. III. 1. 30.
Śrāddhadeva (IV) — Yama; the former birth of Gaveṣuṇa; a destroyer of Indra; father of Ekalavya. Vā. 96. 182.
श्राद्धदेवी: Śrāddhadevī — one of Vasudeva's wives: mother of Ganeṣa. Br. III. 71. 184.
श्राद्धहा: Śrāddhahā — a son of Viṣa. Vā. 68. 33.
श्रावण: Śrāvaṇa (I) — the name of the month and Nakṣatra; god for gift of the Vāyu Purāṇa;1 Kṛṣṇāṣṭamī of this month good for śrāddha.2 1) M. 53. 19; 56. 4; 57. 17; 60. 34; 124. 50. 2) M. 17. 8.
Śrāvaṇa (II) — a son of Gautama, an avatār of the 14th dvāpara. Vā. 23, 164.
श्रावस्त: Śrāvasta — a son of Yuvanāśva and the founder of the city of Śrāvasti; the father of Brahmadaśva. Br. III. 63. 27; M. 12. 30; Vā. 88. 26-7.
श्रावस्ति: Śrāvasti — the city built by Śrāvasta of the Ikṣvāku line; capital of Uttarakośala where Lava ruled;1 in Gauḍa-deśa built by Vatsaka son of Śrāvasta.2 1) Br. III. 63. 28, 200; Vā. 88. 200. 2) M. 12. 30.
श्राविष्ठायन: Śrāviṣṭhāyana — of Śveta Parāśara clan. M. 201. 36.
श्रिंगवान्: Śriṃgavān — a varṣa parvata north of the Śveta of three tops of which one is Iṣuvatam śringa;1 residence of Pitṛs.2 1) Vā. 1. 85; 50. 189. 2) Ib. 46. 35.
श्रिंगि: Śriṃgi — see Śringavān. Br. I. 69; Vā. 64. 7.
श्री: Śrī (I) — (Khāyāti), a daughter of Bhṛgu and Khyāti devoted to Bhagavān;1 requested by Devas to approach Nṛsimha with a view to appease his wrath, she dared not go near him;2 elder sister of Dhātā and Vidhātā; married Nārā-yaṇa and gave birth to Bala and Unmāda (utsāha) besides mind-born sons;3 alias Mahālakṣmī or Lakṣmī.4 1) Bhā. I. 10. 26; 11. 26 and 33; IV. 1. 43; 24. 49. 2) Ib. VII. 9. 2; VIII. 4. 20; 5. 40; 23. 6; IX. 4. 60; X. 3. 50; 9. 20; 29. 37; 31. 17; XI. 14. 15 & 39; XII. 11. 20. 3) Br. II. 11. 2; 13. 78; Vā. 28. 2. 4) Br. IV. 39. 70-71. 44. 71; Vā. 37. 38.
Śrī (II) — came out of the churning of the milk ocean, whom Viṣṇu placed on his breast: the dweller in the lotus: also Śrīdevī. Br. IV. 9. 76, 79; 33. 46; 36. 21, 31 and 90.
Śrī (III) — a Kala of the moon. Br. IV. 35. 92.
श्रीकण्ठ: Śrīkaṇṭha — see Śiva. Br. III. 24. 63; 25. 19; IV. 30. 40.
श्रीखण्ड: Śrīkhaṇḍa — a name for camphor. M. 284. 9.
श्रीगिरि: Śrīgiri — sages of this Mt. visited Dvārakā. Bhā. X. 90. 28[3].
श्रीगुरु: Śrīguru and Gurupatnī — represent Brahmam. Br. IV. 43. 7.
श्रीचक्रम्: Śrīcakram — the mantra of: is Mahālakṣmī: worshipped by Viṣṇu, Śiva and Brahmā: propitiation of, makes one learned: Icon of: the mudras in connection with the worship of; Dīkṣa and its methods. Br. IV. 41. 3-5; chh. 42-3.
श्रीचीन्तामणिमन्त्र: Śrīcīntāmaṇimantra — to be uttered in Devi's offering. Br. IV. 43. 19.
श्रीतलम्: Śrītalam — of rocky earth; here are cities of Kesari, Suparvaṇa, Vāsuki, the king of the Nāgas. Vā. 50. 12, 38-40.
श्रीदण्डनाथा: Śrīdaṇḍanāthā — the leader of Lalitā's hosts against Bhaṇḍa; also Potrinī; her march described; in Kiricakra-ratha: Her mount was the lion Vajraghoṣa;1 hit Kuṭalākṣa, the chief commander of Bhaṇḍa: consulted Mantrinī: helped Kumārī in her expedition against sons of Bhaṇḍa: ascended Geyacakra and fought with Viṣanga: became happy at the end.2 1) Br. IV. 16. 31; 17. 8, 27; ch. 21. 2) Ib. IV. 26. 1-113; 27. 45 and 58; 28. 14-20; 34. 55.
श्रीदामन्: Śrīdāman — a playmate of Kṛṣṇa in his Hariṇākāiḍana sport. Expressed to Kṛṣṇa the desire to rid the palmyra grove of Asura Dhenuka. Being victor in a game, he had the honour of being borne on the back by Kṛṣṇa;1 was placed by Śiva on his lap as a token of affection.2 1) Bhā. X. 15. 20; 18. 23-4; 22. 31; Vi. V. 9. 13-14. 2) Br. III. 42. 55; 43. 29.
श्रीदेवा: Śrīdevā — a daughter of Devaka; a queen of Vasudeva and mother of six sons of whom Nandaka was one. Bhā. IX. 24. 23 & 51; Br. III. 71. 131, 162 and 181; IV. 29. 2; Vā. 96. 130; Vi. 14. 18.
श्रीधर: Śrīdhara — a name of Viṣṇu. Vā. 111. 21.
श्रिपति: Śripati tīrtham — sacred to the Pitṛs. M. 22. 74.
श्रिपर्णि: Śriparṇi — a R. sacred to the Pitṛs. M. 22. 49.
श्रिपर्वतम्: Śriparvatam — Mt. a hill in India, fit for Śrāddha offer-ings;1 sacred to Śiva.2 1) Br. II. 16. 23; III. 13. 28, 31; Vā. 45. 92; 77. 28. 2) M. 181. 28.
श्रीपादुकास्मृति: Śrīpādukāsmṛti — superior to mahādānas and mahā-yajñas. Br. IV. 43. 57.
श्रीपार्वतीय: Śrīpārvatīyas — foresters? ruled for 52 years. M. 273. 23.
श्रीपाशायुधसम्भव: Śrīpāśāyudhasambhava — he who came out of the Pāśa of Lalitā rode on a superior horse. Br. IV. 16. 14 and 29.
श्रिपुरम्: Śripuram — (Śrīnagara) the city of Lalitā: built by Viśvakarman and Maya; in the Ṣoḍaśakṣetra madhya: Of this nine were bhauma and the seven waters: It is called Kāmeśvarīpurī, Bhayamalīpuri, Nityaklinnapuri: surround-ed by Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva lokas: seven prākāras, all of metal. Br. IV. 30. 106-7; 31. 1, 106; 32. 1-10.
श्रीपूर्ति: Śrīpūrti — a devī in Cintāmaṇi gṛha. Br. IV. 36. 26.
श्रीभानु: Śrībhānu — a son of Kṛṣṇa and Satyabhāmā. Bhā. X. 61. 11.
श्रीभूशक्ति: Śrībhūśakti — on the Geyacakra. Br. IV. 19. 74.
श्रिमद्भागवत: Śrimadbhāgavata — produced by the great sage Vyāsa; taught by him to Śuka who narrated it to Parīkṣit, when Sūta heard it. Bhā. I. 1. 2; 3. 40-44.
श्रिमल्लकर्णि: Śrimallakarṇi — a son of Kṛṣṇa, ruled for 10 years. M. 273. 3.
श्रीमहापादुका: Śrīmahāpādukā — in the Cintāmaṇi gṛha. Br. IV. 36. 26.
श्रीमान्: Śrīmān (I) — the most celebrated among the Nīpas. M. 49. 53.
श्रिमान्: Śrimān (II) — a son of Āpa, the Vasava. M. 203. 6.
श्रीमूर्ति: Śrīmūrti — the manifestation of Hari in the epoch of the tenth Manu: born of Viśvasrk. Bhā. VIII. 13. 21[1].
श्रीरङ्ग: Śrīraṅga — visited by Balarāma;1 sacred to Pitṛs.2 1) Bhā. X. 79. 14. 2) M. 22. 44.
श्रीवत्स: Śrīvatsa — the jewel of Kṛṣṇa;1 of Pauṇḍarīka Vāsudeva.2 1) Vā. 96. 204. 2) Vi. V. 34. 17.
श्रीवनम्: Śrīvanam — a bilvavanam east of Ś(r)īsaras; served by the Gandharvas, Kinnaras, Yakṣas, Siddhas; the residence of Śrī. Vā. 37. 13-15.
श्रीवृक्ष: Śrīvṛkṣa — near the Cītrakūṭa hill fit for Śrāddha.12 1) Br. III. 13. 38. 2) Vā. 77. 38.
श्रिवृक्षक: Śrivṛkṣaka — a palace; see Padmaka. M. 269. 44.
श्रीशान्तकर्ण: Śrīśāntakarṇa(i) — a son of Kṛṣṇa, and father of Paurṇa-māsa: ruled for 56 years. Bhā. XII. 1. 23; Br. III. 74. 162.
श्रीसूक्तम्: Śrīsūktam — in honour of Śrī;1 to be uttered when found-ing temples.2 1) Br. IV. 9. 77; Vi. I. 9. 101. 2) M. 265. 24.
श्रीशैल: Śrīśaila — a Mt in Bhārata varṣa, sacred to Śiva. Rukmī addressed himself to this god: visited by Balarāma;1 sacred to Lalitāpīṭha;2 sacred to Goddess Mahādevī and the Pitṛs;3 a part of the burning Tripura fell there.4 1) Bhā. V. 19. 16; X. 61. 23[1]; 79. 13. 2) Br. IV. 44. 98. 3) M. 13. 31; 22. 43. 4) Ib. 188. 79.
श्रीसोमनाथ: Śrīsomanātha — Candra (s.v.) arising out of Atri's eyes: 27 nakṣatras being his śaktis. Br. IV. 35. 54-5.
श्रुत: Śruta (I) — a son of Bhagiratha (Suhotra-Vi. P.) and father of Nābha(ga). Bhā. IX. 9. 16; Br. III. 63. 169; Vā. 88. 160; Vi. IV. 4. 36.
Śruta (II) — a son of Subhāṣaṇa, and father of Jaya. Bhā. IX. 13. 25.
Śruta (III) — a son of Kṛṣṇa and Kālindī. Bhā. X. 61. 14.
Śruta (IV) — a son of Medhā. Br. II. 9. 59; Vā. 10. 35.
Śruta (V) — a son of Svārociṣa Manu. Br. II. 36. 19.
Śruta (VI) — a son of Suvarca. Vā. 89. 21.
श्रुतऋषि: Śrutaṛṣi — a learned Purāṇa reader. Vā. 99. 417.

Śrutaṛṣis — 8000 in number, are born again and again and take up the arrangement of the Śamhitās;1 remembered 88,000 Samhitās which return again and again.2 1) Br. II. 33. 2; 35. 146; M. 145. 88. 2) Vā. 59. 86; 61. 122.
श्रुतकर्मन्: Śrutakarman (I) — a son of Sahadeva and Draupadī. Bhā. IX. 22. 30; M. 50. 52; Vi. IV. 20. 42.
Śrutakarman (II) — a son of Chāyā and Mārtāṇḍa (sun); became later Śanaiścara. Br. III. 59. 48; Vā. 84. 50.
श्रुतकीर्ति: Śrutakīrti (I) — a son of Arjuna and Draupadī. Bhā. IX. 22. 29; M. 50. 52; Vi. IV. 20. 42.
श्रुतकीर्ती: Śrutakīrtī (II) — a daughter of Sura1 (Śūra and Bhojā-M. P.) and queen of Dhṛṣṭaketu Kaikeya; a paternal aunt of Kṛṣṇa, and mother of Bhadrā, married to Kṛṣṇa; also mother of Anuvrata (Santardanā-Vi. P.) besides four other sons; a viramātā.2 1) Br. III. 71. 150 & 57; 2) Bhā. IX. 24. 30 and 38; X. 58. 56; M. 46. 4-5; Vā. 96. 149; 156. 7; Vi. IV. 14. 31, 41-2.
श्रुतदेव: Śrutadeva (I) — a Brahman follower of Kṛṣṇa; knew his yoga power; lived as householder in Mithilā, earning bread for the day and contented; was visited by Kṛṣṇa and was happy at the honour done to him. Bhā. I. 14. 32; II. 7. 45; X. 78. [95 (v) 1]; 86. 13 to 57.
Śrutadeva (II) — a siddha; attacked the Asura followers of Bali. Bhā. VI. 15. 15; VIII. 21. 17; X. 86. 13.
Śrutadeva (III) — a son of Kṛṣṇa. Bhā. X. 90. 34.
श्रुतदेवा: Śrutadevā — a daughter of Śūra; a sister of Vasudeva; wife of Vṛddhaśaman Kārūṣa (Vṛddhadharma, the kārūśa king-Vi. P.) mother of Dantavaktra (the great Asura). Bhā. IV. 24. 30 and 37; Br. III. 71; 150 and 156; Vā. 96. 149, 155; Vi. IV. 14. 31, 39, 40.
श्रुतदेवी: Śrutadevī — a daughter of Devaka and one of the seven wives of Vasudeva. M. 44. 73.
श्रुतधर: Śrutadhara — the companion who followed Puramjana to Uttara and Dakṣiṇa Pāñcāla; allegorically, the hearing. Bhā. IV. 25. 50-51; 29. 13.
Śrutadharas — a class of people in Śālmalidvīpa. Bhā. V. 20. 11.
श्रुतंजय: Śrutaṃjaya (I) — a son of Satyāyu. Bhā. IX. 15. 2.
Śrutaṃjaya (II) — a Bṛhadratha; ruled for 24 years. Br. III. 74. 114.
Śrutaṃjaya (III) — ruled for 40 years. M. 271. 23; Vā. 99. 300.
श्रुतवर्मन्: Śrutavarman — a minister of Bhaṇḍa. Br. IV. 12. 53.
श्रुतविन्दा: Śrutavindā — a R. in Kuśadvīpa. Bhā. V. 20. 15.
श्रुतश्रवस्: Śrutaśravas (I) — a son of Somāpī;1 ruled for 67 years;2 father of Ayutāyu.3 1) Bhā. IX. 22. 9. 2) Br. III. 74. 111. 3) Vi. IV. 23. 4.
Śrutaśravas (II) — a son of Mārjāri, and father of Ayu-tāyu. Bhā. IX. 22. 46.

Śrutaśravas (III) — a daughter of Śūra and Bhojā;1 a sister of Vasudeva and queen of Damaghoṣa, the Cedi king;2 mother of Śisupāla; a Vīramātā.3 1) M. 46. 4, 6. 2) Bhā. IX. 24. 30 and 39; Br. III. 71. 150 and 158; Vi. IV. 14. 31, 44-5. 3) Vā. 96. 149, 157-8.
Śrutaśravas (IV) — a son of Chāyā and the Sun god; was Sāvarṇi Manu. Br. III. 59. 48; Vā. 84. 50.
Śrutaśravas (V) — a son of Somavit. M. 50. 34.

Śrutaśravas (VI) — (Māgadha) in the line of Somādhi (tasyānvaya) ruled for 64 years; this gap between Somādhi and Śrutaśravas seems to account for the discrepancy be-tween the names given and the total No. 32 of the kings. M. 271. 20; Vā. 99. 228, 297.
श्रुतसेन: Śrutasena (I) — a son of Śatrughna. Bhā. IX. 11. 12.
Śrutasena (II) — a son of Bhīma and Draupadī. Bhā. IX. 22. 29; M. 50. 52; Vi. IV. 20. 42.
Śrutasena (III) — a son of Parīkṣit. Bhā. IX. 22. 35; Vi. IV. 20. 1; 21. 3.
श्रुतादेवी: Śrutādevī — a daughter of Śūra and Bhojā, wife of Kṛta, and mother of Sugrīva. M. 46. 4-5.
श्रुतानीक: Śrutānīka — a son of Nakula by Draupadī. Vi. IV. 20. 42.
श्रुतायुस्: Śrutāyus (I) — a son of Ariṣṭanemi and father of Supār-śva(ka). Bhā. IX. 13. 23; Vi. IV. 5. 31.
Śrutāyus (II) — a son of Purūravas and Ūrvaśī. Father of Vasumat. Bhā. IX. 15. 1 and 2; Br. III. 66. 23; Vi. IV. 7. 1.
Śrutāyus (III) — a Vānara chief. Br. III. 7. 236.
Śrutāyus (IV) — a son of Bhānuścandra, was slain in the Bhārata battle. M. 12. 55.
श्रुतार्थकृत्: Śrutārthakṛt — a son of Jāmbavān. Br. III. 7. 303.
श्रुति: Śruti (I) — the Vedas: interpreted in two ways in the Dvāpara;1 the same, Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma in every manvan-tara though in different redactions; here are four stotras — Dravyastotram, Guṇastotram, Karmastotram, and Abhi-janastotram; above all these is Brahmastotram; mantras were originally five fold;2 having learnt the Śrauta from their predecessors the seven sages repeated the same.3 1) Br. II. 31. 6, 72; 32, 35; IV. 6. 64; M. 52. 12; 144. 7; Vā. 34. 95; 39. 11; 41. 90; 55. 7; 61. 75; 76. 3; 100. 33; 101. 9, 22, 57. 2) M. 145. 58-63. 3) Vā. 3. 8; 32. 44; 59. 31.
Śruti (II) — a son of Uttama Manu. Br. II. 36. 40.
Śruti (III) — a daughter of Anasūyā and mother of Śankhapadā, wife of Kardama, Pulaha Prajāpati. Vā. 28. 18, 27; Br. II. 11. 22.
Śrutis — awaken the Lord sleeping after a pralaya, as bards the emperor from his bed. Śrutigītā on the greatness and glory of Lord. Bhā. V. 87. 1, 12-41; XI. 5. 5.
श्रुतिकेवल: Śrutikevala — a ṛtvik at Brahmā's sacrifice. Vā. 106. 35.
श्रुतिपराग: Śrutiparāga — one of Bhaṇḍa's eight men. Br. IV. 12. 12.
श्रुतिश्रव: Śrutiśravas — a son of Somapa; the last of the Māgadhas. Vi. IV. 19. 84-5.
शृंगवत्: Śṛṃgavat — a Mt. range to the north of Ilāvṛta; a boundary limit of Kuru; from it descends the stream Bhadrā. Bhā. V. 16. 8; 17. 8.
श्रेणि: Śreṇis — military republics;1 treated with respect by Pṛthu; help kings.2 1) M. 273. 68. 2) Bhā. IV. 17. 2; Br. III. 7. 264.
श्रेयोव्रतम्: Śreyovratam — leads to Śiva, salvation. M. 101. 70.
श्रेष्ट: Śreṣṭa — a Sudhāmāna god. Br. II. 36. 28.
श्रोणी: Śroṇī — a R. of the Bhāratavarṣa. Vā. 45. 100.
श्रोत: Śrota — the Yakṣa presiding over the month, Nabha. Bhā. XII. 11. 37.
श्रोतामन्त: Śrotāmanta — a god of Ādya group. Br. II. 36. 69.
श्रोतोगुणात्मक: Śrotoguṇātmakas — the three guṇas, satva, rajas and tamas revolve round and round among all worldly creatures. Vā. 102. 56.
श्रोत्रम्: Śrotram — a Tuṣita god. Br. III. 3. 19. Vā. 66. 18.
श्रोत्रि: Śrotri — guides the month of Nabhas. Bhā. XII. 11. 37.
श्रोत्रीय: Śrotrīya — eligible for Pārvaṇa śrāddha, as also his son. M. 16. 8; 105. 17; Vi. III. 15. 2.
श्रौत: Śrauta — from śravaṇa — to hear or heard; principally of the sacrifice and Veda. Vā. 59. 38.
श्रौतगेपि: Śrautagepi — an Ārṣeya Pravara of the Bhārgavas. M. 195. 38.
श्रौतम्: Śrautam Dharmam and Smārta — promulgated by the seven sages and Manu at the commencement of the Tretā yuga;1 two-fold, dhārāgnihotrasambandham said in four days; hearing is śrauta;2 lost in Arājaka;3 the śruta consists of mar-riage, agnihotra, and Vedic studies; this is according to the Sapta ṛṣis.4 1) Br. II. 29. 44-51; 32. 33-5. 2) Ib. II. 32. 33-5, 43, 44; III. 21. 47. 3) Ib. II. 31. 95. 4) Vā. 57. 39-40.
श्रौतस्मार्तम्: Śrautasmārtam — commences with Tretāyuga; originally told by seven sages;1 it is called jñānadharma; characteristics of; the one deals with sacrifices and the other with Var-ṇāśrama;2 is lost towards the close of Kali (in Kali).3 1) M. 142. 40. 2) Ib. 144. 96; 145. 22, 30-31, 40. 3) Ib. 273. 46; Vi. IV. 24. 98.
श्वनरक: Śvanaraka — a kind of hell. Vā. 101. 149.
श्वपाक: Śvapākas — Caṇḍālas; with minds controlled and resign-ed to Hari are better than Brahmans not devoted to God; were honoured by Kṛṣṇa; become pure by bhakti (also śvāda s.v.);1 meat eaters with whom Satyavrata-Triśanku lived.2 1) Bhā. I. 11. 22; VII. 9. 10; XI. 14. 21. 2) Br. III. 63. 81; Vā. 88. 82.
श्वफल्क: Śvaphalka — a son of Vṛṣṇi; elder brother of Citraka; married Gāndinī, daughter of a Kāśī king. Akrūra was the foremost of his twelve sons. Kāśī, not visited by rains for long had a heavy shower just at his marriage, and during his stay at the invitation of the Kāśī king, whose daughter he married. A righteous king in whose kingdom there was neither famine nor disease. Bhā. III. 1. 32; IX. 24. 15; X. 38. 24; 57. 32; XI. 12. 10; Br. III. 71, 102; Vi. IV. 13. 115-16; 15. 5-7.
श्वभोजन: Śvabhojana — a hell; the abode of Vratins and Brahma-cārins with an uncontrolled body, taught and disciplined by sons, and Brahmacāris that sleep during day time. Br. IV. 2. 149, 176; Vā. 101. 148, 173; Vi. II. 6. 5 and 29.
श्वमुख: Śvamukhas — the country of, watered by Nalinī. Br. II. 18. 60.
श्वर: Śvara — a son of Dadhīci. Vā. 21. 42.
श्वशृप: Śvaśṛpa — a nephew of Hiraṇyakaśipu. M. 6. 27.
श्वा: Śvā — unfit to be seen during a śrāddha; touching it is a sin. Br. III. 14. 48; 78, 88; 27. 15; Vi. III. 16. 12.
श्वाजित: Śvājita (Ātreya) — a sage of the epoch of Bhautya Manu. Br. IV. 1. 114.
श्वात: Śvāta — a son of Brahmadhāna. Br. III. 7. 98.
श्वाद: Śvāda — (also Śvapaca) — see Śvapākas. Bhā. III 33. 6 and 7.
श्वान: Śvāna — a Rudra on the Ṣoḍaśa cakra. Br. IV. 34. 26.
श्वानबलि: Śvānabali — oblation to dogs; Syāma and Śabala. Vā. 111. 39.
श्वापद: Śvāpada — the Asura whose city is in Tatvalam. Br. II. 20. 18.
श्वापदनगरम्: Śvāpadanagaram — in the first tala of the Atalam. Vā. 50. 17.
श्वाहि: Śvāhi — a son of Vṛjinivata, and father of Ruśaku. Bhā. IX. 23. 31.
श्वेत: Śveta (I) — (Varṣaparvata) a Mt. range to the north of Ilāvṛta, and a boundary limit of Hiraṇmaya; residence of Daityas and Dānavas; centres round the Kumuda hill of Śālmalidvīpam; for Asuras. Bhā. V. 16. 8; Br. II. 1. 69; II. 15. 22 and 28; 17. 35; 20. 52; III. 7. 194; M. 113. 23, 84; 144. 57; Vā. 1. 85; 42. 68; 45. 2; 46. 35. 49. 39; 50. 50.
Śveta (II) — a chief Nāga of Pātāla;1 with the sun in Āvaṇi and Puraṭṭāśi.2 1) Bhā. V. 24. 31. 2) Br. II. 23. 10; Vā. 52. 11.
Śveta (III) — a son of Vapuṣmat after whom came the Śvetadeśa. Br. II. 14. 32-3; Vā. 33. 28; Vi. II. 4. 23, 29.
Śveta (IV) — a son of Devajanī and a Yakṣa. Br. III. 7. 128.
Śveta (V) — a son of Bṛhati. Br. III. 71. 256; Vā. 96. 247.
Śveta (VI) — a son of Vipracitta the dānava in the Tāra-kāmaya war. M. 173. 19; 177. 7.

Śveta (VII) — the form of a great seer which Śiva as-sumes at the end of the four Yugas of the Kalpa; (Vārāha) in the Chagala hillock of the Himālayas;1 the avatār of the 23rd dvāpara in the Kalañjara hill.2 1) Vā. 23. 115. 2) Ib. 23. 203-4.
Śveta (VIII) — one of the four Vedic disciples of Śveta, an avatār of the Lord Śiva. Vā. 23. 117.
Śveta (IX) — a son of Maṇivara. Vā. 69. 159.
Śveta (X) — a ṛtvik at Brahmā's sacrifice. Vā. 106. 36.
Śveta (XI) — a division of Jambūdvipa. Vi. II. 1. 21. 2. 11.
Śveta cakṣu — a god of Prasūta group. Br. II. 36. 70.
Śvetas (I) — a Parāśara clan; a dynasty of kings. Br. III. 8. 95; 74. 268; Vā. 70. 89; 73. 62.
Śvetas (II) — the sages who sprang out of the side of Kumāra (Deveśa) in the 29th Kalpa. Vā. 22. 15.
Śvetas (III) — a Janapada of the Ketumālā. Vā. 44. 11; 99. 455.
श्वेतकल्प: Śvetakalpa — the first kalpa; explained in the Vāyavya Purāṇa;1 Dharmavṛtā performed tapas in and became turned to a stone;2 Vārāha in;3 Śiva takes the avatār of Sad-yojāta, all white, when Gāyatrī also is born with him.4 1) M. 290. 3; 53. 18. 2) Vā. 107. 6. 3) Ib. 105. 7; 106. 32; 109. 35. 4) Ib. 23. 63.
श्वेतकेतु: Śvetaketu (II) — a son of Lāngali, an avatār of the Lord. Vā. 23. 200.
श्वेतद्वीप: Śvetadvīpa — sacred to Hari, visited by Nārada. Bhā. VIII. 4. 18; X. 6. 24; 87. 10; XI. 15. 18.
श्वेतपर्वा: Śvetaparvā — burnt by Śiva's anger and reattained divi-nity with Cupid. M. 191. 112.
श्वेतम्: Śvetam — a region of Śālmalidvīpa adjoining the Kumuda hill;1 the kingdom of Hiraṇvān.2 1) Br. II. 19. 44. 2) Ib. II. 14. 50; 15. 34; 19. 44.
श्वेतरत: Śvetarata — a son of Hṛdika. Br. III. 71. 14.
श्वेतलोहित: Śvetalohita (I) — 29th kalpa; out of contemplation of Brahmā came into being Kumāra along with seers known as śvetas, disciple of Brahmā, Sunanda, etc., besides the great sage Śveta. Vā. 22. 9-20.
Śvetalohita (II) — a disciple of Śveta avatār of Śiva. Vā. 23. 117.
श्वेतवर्ण: Śvetavarṇa — a Kulaparvata of the Bhadrāśva. Vā. 43. 14.
श्वेतवाहन: Śvetavāhana (I) — a son of Śūra. Br. III. 71. 138; Vā. 96. 136.
Śvetavāhana (II) — a son of Rājādhideva. M. 44. 78.
श्वेता: Śvetā (I) — a daughter of Krodhavaśā (Krodhā-Vā. P.) and wife of Pulaha; mother of Vānaras;1 mother of four Diggajas.2 1) Br. III. 7. 172, 180-203; Vā. 69. 205. 2) Vā. 69. 214.
Śvetā (II) — a daughter of Bṛhati. Br. III. 7. 256; Vā. 96. 247.
श्वेतांग: Śvetāṃgas — a Janapada of the Ketumālā continent. Vā. 44. 11.
श्वेताम्बुज: Śvetāmbujas — a class of gods doing śrāddha. Br. III. 10. 109.
श्वेताश्व: Śvetāśva — one of the four learned Brahman disciples of Śveta. Vā. 23. 117.
श्वेतोदर: Śvetodara — a Mt. on the south of the Mānasa. Vā. 36. 23; 39. 56; 42. 30.
शुकृत: Śukṛta (I) — a son of Vasiṣṭha and a Prajāpati of the Svārociṣa epoch. M. 9. 9.
शुष्मन्त: Śuṣmanta — a son of Trasa. Vā. 99. 133.
शूचीदर्भ: Śūcīdarbhas — the kingdom of Suvīra. Vā. 99. 24.
शूर्यकान्त: Śūryakānta — a Kulaparvata of the Uttara Kuru country. Vā. 45. 25.
